posts.text:
I kept typing Russian with the English layout still on.

ghbdtn. cgfcb,j. Every single day.

So I built Rekey: it notices the word came out on the wrong layout and fixes it as you type. Free, open source, runs entirely on your machine.

macOS + Windows: {repo}

The hard part of a layout switcher isn't catching mistakes. It's not creating them.

Being right 95% of the time is fine until the other 5% lands in a password field.

Rekey changed 0.00% of correctly-typed words across 54,000 tests.

{repo}

Dictionaries don't contain "норм", "чувак", "gonna" or "lol".

So Rekey's language models are trained on subtitle corpora instead — transcribed speech, full of the words people actually type.

yjhv xedfr → норм чувак

{repo}

Rekey reads every key you press. What it does with them:

Nothing leaves your machine. No telemetry, no account, no network calls. The language models ship inside the app — 4.6 MB for ten languages.

It's MIT licensed, so you can check.

{repo}

Rekey speaks five scripts properly: Cyrillic, Hebrew, Arabic, Greek and Latin.

Russian, Ukrainian, Hebrew, Arabic and Greek all run 88–99% accuracy with zero false positives.

akuo → שלום

{repo}

An honest limitation, published on our own landing page:

Rekey barely helps with Spanish or German.

Spanish and US QWERTY produce identical letters for a–z. Only ñ and the accents differ. There's almost nothing to detect.

{repo}

A bug I enjoyed finding.

Rekey skips ALL-CAPS words — usually acronyms. The check: no character is lowercase.

Hebrew and Arabic have no lowercase. Every word in both read as SHOUTING.

Both scored 0% until I fixed it.

{repo}

Greek detection sat at 4.8% and I couldn't see why.

Greek accents are dead keys, so a mistyped Greek word contains a semicolon — and my filter threw those out as "not a word".

One fix later: 95.8%.

{repo}

Russian б and ю live on the , and . keys.

So "спасибо" typed on a US layout comes out as cgfcb,j — commas and all.

Any switcher that filters input to "letters only" discards the exact words it exists to fix.

{repo}

Rekey never swallows a keystroke.

The character you typed always lands first. Corrections come after, as ordinary backspaces and text.

That's why it works in every app — editors, browsers, chat — without integrating with any.

{repo}

Every automatic correction needs a one-key undo, or people stop trusting it.

In Rekey, undoing a correction also teaches it: that word is never auto-corrected again.

Disagreeing with the tool once should be enough.

{repo}

If an app watches your keyboard, "trust me" isn't good enough.

Rekey is MIT licensed, builds from source in three commands, and the accuracy numbers on the site are reproducible with one:

cargo run -p eval

{repo}
